title: Code of conduct policy approved without attire list
subtitle: Heritage permit for 54 Albert Street, elected officials' expenses report, fire protection agreement with Wilmot, traffic by-law, Earth Day cleanups.
overview: Council approved the new H-004 Code of Conduct Policy {{vote:m4}}, after amending it to remove the list of unacceptable clothing and footwear from section 3.13. Staff will update the policy and cover questions about appropriate attire through training. The policy replaces a document about 20 years old and applies to City employees.

Council also approved a heritage permit for 54 Albert Street, subject to conditions in the staff report {{vote:m3}}, and received the annual statement of remuneration and expenses for elected officials as information {{vote:m5}}.

Council enacted three by-laws in one motion {{vote:m6}}. These authorize a fire protection agreement between the City and the Township of Wilmot, amend the by-law regulating traffic and parking on highways under City jurisdiction, and confirm the actions of the meeting.

Before the open meeting, Council met in closed session on labour relations with the WPFFA. The minutes report no public decision from that session. One councillor also encouraged residents to sign up for Earth Day cleanups in April.

decisions.detail: Council approved the updated policy with the list of unacceptable attire removed from section 3.13, and directed staff to update it as required.
Council approved heritage permit application HP2022-015 subject to the conditions in section 3.0 of staff report IPPW2023-019.
Council received the annual statement of remuneration and expenses for elected officials (CORP2023-012) as information.

debate: One councillor asked to remove the list of unacceptable attire because the policy already calls for business attire, making the list redundant, and argued that discretion in applying the policy would be better.

The same councillor said some items on the list, such as tank tops and running shoes, can be appropriate in some settings, and did not want removal to lead to the same restrictions being applied elsewhere.
Staff said questions about appropriate attire could be handled through the training that will accompany the policy, while noting that enforcement needs to be consistent across the organization.
Staff also said that if specific clothing items were a concern, they could take that feedback back and consider it when preparing training.
